subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Acidity in Coffee
description: A quick win: understand Acidity in Coffee.

hook.text: Acidity in coffee isn't about pH. It's the bright, lively sensation that makes great coffee taste vibrant.

buildup.text: Citric acid tastes lemony. Malic acid tastes apple-like. Phosphoric gives a sparkling, cola-like brightness.

discovery.text: High-altitude beans develop more organic acids because slow ripening concentrates these compounds.

twist.text: Dark roasting destroys most acids. That's why dark roasts taste flatter and less complex than light roasts.

climax.text: Acidity is the backbone of specialty coffee. Without it, coffee tastes dull—like music without treble.

punchline.text: Not sour. Bright. Acidity is coffee's sparkle.

quiz.question: Why do high-altitude beans have more acidity?

details.summary: Acidity in coffee is a desirable quality that creates brightness, liveliness, and complexity in the cup. It is not the same as sourness, which indicates under-extraction. Citric, malic, and phosphoric acids contribute fruity, green apple, and sparkling qualities respectively.
details.whyItMatters: Acidity is one of the primary attributes professional tasters evaluate. Learning to appreciate it transforms how you experience quality coffee.
takeaways: Acidity adds brightness and complexity to coffee flavor
Citric acid creates citrus notes; malic acid adds apple character
High-altitude coffees tend to have greater acidity

faq.question: Is acidic coffee bad for your stomach?
faq.answer: Coffee's acidity is similar to orange juice at a pH of around 5. Most people tolerate it well. Those with acid reflux may benefit from low-acid varieties, darker roasts, or cold brew, all of which have reduced perceived acidity.

faq.question: What is the difference between acidity and sourness?
faq.answer: Acidity is a pleasant, bright sensation like biting into a ripe fruit. Sourness is harsh, puckering, and unpleasant, usually caused by under-extraction. Good acidity enhances flavor; sourness indicates a brewing problem.
